product_families.name: SmokeFire

observations.exact_model: Weber Connect controller (diagnostic label; SKU not independently recorded)
observations.notes: Targeted app-closed readings and automatic recovery after owner-controlled power cycling and a move from Probe 4 to Probe 2; 18 entity identities preserved. Eleven post-recovery minutes had no new failures. No independently timed power-on latency, actual token-expiry trial, on-wire capture, full stable matrix or other-family qualification.
Maintainer receipt records an ESPHome 2026.7.0 proxy, Home Assistant 2026.7.2, Android app coexistence, probe readings and bounded cook/proxy endurance. Bound to 3.0.0-rc only.

observations.exact_model: Performer Deluxe Smart 57 / Performer Premium Smart
observations.notes: The report says the built-in grill-temperature entity and external probes worked, and the model has two physical probe ports. It is not a controlled endurance or current-release test.

Community comment reports a 3.5-hour manual cook with the Android app open, restart recovery and stable IDs/nicknames. It also reports fuel changes and two cloud gaps; endurance is not marked passed. Bound to RC3 only.

Empty-grill manual trial on HA 2026.10.2, firmware 2.0.3_7398, app open and BLE proxy off: cooking/model/warnings corrected, stable IDs, real low/full agrees, all three cloud gaps self-recovered. Fuel flicker and 2-5.5 minute gaps remain; no controlled endurance pass or RC5 acceptance.

Contributor reports a 3h 15m cook with grill/target and two wired probe temperatures, median updates around 11 seconds and a longest gap of 1.5 minutes. Pairing required about 12 attempts with encrypted-response, reachability and connection errors. Fuel, probe targets and intensity were absent and the model was labeled Hub. Restart, reconnect, stable IDs and app coexistence were not tested; this is not full acceptance or evidence for 3.3.

feedback.summary: Cooking appeared off during an active manual SmokeFire cook.
feedback.disposition: During the November 26 RC1 cook, cooking appeared off and device state idle for about 51 minutes while connection and probes stayed active. A grill setpoint change restored the state. No raw frame history identifies whether a new cook boundary occurred or the status was incomplete. The cause remains open pending timestamped device-state and cook-mode evidence during the false idle interval.

feedback.summary: SmokeFire appeared with a generic Hub model label.
feedback.disposition: RC4 uses observed model evidence or a recognized SmokeFire title. Its community trial confirms the SmokeFire label; 3.3.0rc13 hardware regression remains pending.

feedback.summary: Certificate loading could block Home Assistant setup.
feedback.disposition: HTTPS opener creation is deferred into the executor request path. The RC4 reporter confirms the blocking-SSL warning disappeared; 3.3.0rc13 physical regression is pending.

feedback.summary: A deprecated unscoped device lookup was reported.
feedback.disposition: Firmware updates use a config-entry-scoped lookup compatible with the HA baseline. The RC4 reporter confirms the deprecated-registry warning disappeared; 3.3.0rc13 physical regression is pending.

feedback.summary: SmokeFire fuel reports changed between full and unknown during the community run.
feedback.disposition: The November 26 RC1 real-cook report counted 332 full-fuel reports and zero unknown/invalid reports while Home Assistant showed repeated full-to-unknown-to-full transitions. RC13 removes healthy-socket expiry between unchanged reports. Explicit values still apply immediately, and inherited values expire after 60 seconds across socket close/reconnect. The regression passes locally. A cook on this candidate is pending.

feedback.summary: SmokeFire cooking-time cloud gaps last multiple minutes despite automatic recovery.
feedback.disposition: The November 26 RC1 real-cook report describes eight cloud connection gaps, all automatically recovered, while the Weber app kept updating during two checked gaps and other cloud services remained healthy. This does not identify the failing path or establish a code-level cloud-gap fix. Keep the cause unresolved.

feedback.summary: Genesis issue 65 reports a response-framing failure after controller discovery.
feedback.disposition: SiLabs classification and setup are implemented, but no successful reporter pairing, physical approval, cloud association or live reading is recorded. Do not relax framing without sanitized controller evidence and a regression fixture.

feedback.summary: EP-series thermometer showed the approval prompt, but the RC12 pairing attempt timed out after the user confirmed it.
feedback.disposition: On RC12, the reporter saw the approval prompt and captured the pairing-response notification after confirming it. Its appliance counter (28, boot count 2) differed from request counter 1. The reported 83-byte notification length is ambiguous because the header declares 83 payload bytes, which imply 90 bytes including the header. RC12 incorrectly required matching counters. RC13 accepts by outstanding message type and performs a solicited GATT read for an empty or truncated notification, while preserving frame validation, status/key checks and authenticated handshake. Exact-device pairing, cloud association and telemetry still need hardware confirmation.

feedback.summary: Cloud status stayed connected while Home Assistant stopped receiving readings.
feedback.disposition: The November 26 RC1 diagnostics confirm current cloud status cleared during connection loss. The last device-reported status remained available as historical context. A new socket requires a fresh device report before publishing current cloud status.

feedback.summary: Cloud status repeatedly went unknown while cook telemetry continued.
feedback.disposition: The November 26 RC1 cook recorded 112 transitions to unknown, often around a fuel drop. A timestamped example during healthy telemetry is needed to distinguish socket replacement from a device report.

feedback.summary: Runtime evidence is bound to the exact candidate fingerprint and must not be carried across candidates.
feedback.disposition: RC13 receives a separate runtime fingerprint and pending physical receipt. RC12 and prior hardware observations remain historical and cannot qualify the updated runtime. OEM APK provenance and its offline app display have been reviewed, but do not constitute candidate hardware acceptance.

feedback.summary: HACS review identified device-settings writes inside cloud subscription despite the read-only contract.
feedback.disposition: RC3 continues to reject settings writes and empty program-detail requests. It permits only empty status/capability reads plus an exact two-byte active-probe program read. Requests and responses are bounded and correlated; no cooking or target controls are enabled.

feedback.summary: Searwood pairing required repeated attempts and physical approval was difficult to complete.
feedback.disposition: The 3.2.2 report includes encrypted-response, proxy reachability and connection errors before eventual success. OEM inspection does not establish their cause. Capture sanitized failing-stage/framing evidence and approval timing on the affected controller; do not treat a longer timeout as a proven fix.

feedback.summary: Searwood appears as a Connect Smart Grilling Hub.
feedback.disposition: The existing legacy model label is insufficient for this report. Obtain controller/product metadata before mapping the model; no Searwood-specific identity fix is implemented.

feedback.summary: Searwood did not create fuel or cook-intensity entities.
feedback.disposition: Fuel and intensity decoders and conditional entities already exist in stable 3.2.2 and the candidate. OEM 2.13 mappings agree. Obtain the actual field presence and app values for this controller, including Manual Mode intensity, before changing decoding or declaring support.

feedback.summary: Probe target temperatures are not exposed.
feedback.disposition: RC3 adds scoped read-only program fetching, versioned target parsing, session/step binding and stale-target clearing. Single thresholds and ranges have separate sensor representations. Software checks and the exact-candidate OEM comparison are recorded in the RC3 receipts; other controllers need their own trials.

feedback.summary: Searwood restart, reconnect, stable IDs and app coexistence remain untested.
feedback.disposition: The contributor cook confirms useful 3.2.2 readings but not these lifecycle outcomes. Keep each pending stage separate from the successful cook and from current-candidate acceptance.
